reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about reduction kinetics, nucleation, and segregation, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not establish that millisecond thermal pulses synchronize reduction of multiple noble metal precursors or that this prevents segregation in high-entropy alloys.
premises: Noble metal precursors can be reduced nearly simultaneously by a rapid, synchronized thermal pulse
Synchronized reduction maximizes atomic intermixing and suppresses elemental segregation
Uniform nucleation leads to a homogeneous alloy structure with enhanced surface-atom exposure
Slower heating causes sequential reduction, leading to elemental segregation or phase separation
The mechanism applies to noble metals with comparable reduction potentials under inert atmosphere
